extractions.value: Patient had supranuclear upward gaze palsy and slow saccades, which is described as the first such case in GlyR Ab-positive PERM, suggesting involvement of the rostral midbrain. Bladder voiding remained difficult upon discharge, necessitating intermittent self-catheterization.
extractions.quote: Our present GlyR Ab-positive PERM case is the first with a supranuclear gaze palsy and slow vertical saccades, suggesting involvement of the rostral midbrain... Bladder voiding remained difficult, necessitating intermittent self-catheterization.
